periods.summary: Lunaeyes is Vermillion's first princess and next queen. She is absent from the initial family meeting because of war preparations, but when Ikki climbs into her room by accident she quickly understands the situation, treats his injury, and produces the bounty poster proving Sirius's plot. She had already prepared a national broadcast system to intervene if needed, and uses it to make Ikki's pledge and Sirius's agreement public. She then sets Ikki's condition: participate as a specially summoned representative in the war against Quedolan and bring Vermillion victory. She had negotiated for this in advance with Quedolan's side.

periods.summary: Lunaeyes brings Timid and Milialia to Ikki for training and takes John Cobrand's call requesting a Quedland visit. She travels with Ikki and Stella, explains how Sirius and Astrea transformed centuries of hatred into friendly ceremonial war, and meets John in Luxel. When Or-Gaule reveals his control of Quedland, Lunaeyes tries to evacuate civilians and then attacks him in rage, but is captured and nearly strangled. Alice evacuates her to Freyaveg and she is treated for light hypoxic brain injury and a sprained ankle. Later, to everyone's shock, Lunaeyes appears beside John and Or-Gaule on Golden Chariot, says she voluntarily returned to the current Quedland king, and uses her delegated authority to accept Quedland's declaration as a legal representative war while rejecting League emergency intervention.

periods.summary: Lunaeyes realizes Sirius's nonlethal battlefield order will cost many lives before League reinforcements arrive. She leaves the hospital alone, goes to Quedland, and negotiates with Or-Gaule to convert the conflict into a legal five-on-five representative war, buying time to evacuate citizens while also blocking League intervention. Nene later deduces that ordinary advantage would never move Or-Gaule, implying Lunaeyes paid some terrible personal price, but Lunaeyes refuses to reveal it. On the eve of the war she tries to evacuate the citizens and control Sirius, yet Stella's confidence cracks her rational mask; she finally asks Stella to save John. She then accepts that waiting with the people is her own form of battle.

key_events.summary: Decides to go to Quedland and negotiate a representative war.

periods.summary: Before the war, Lunaeyes summons Sirius and Astrea and formally announces that she will renounce Vermillion's succession because she wants to stay beside John during his worst suffering. She admits that she has tried to frame the decision as political reasoning, but the truth is that she loves John and wants to support him personally. Sirius, despite his loneliness, tells her to go do what only she can do. During the battle, Lunaeyes appears in the devastated outskirts where Stella's slap sent John. She reminds John of a childhood promise: if he cannot bear the burden of kingship alone, she will help carry it; if he cannot endure the pain alone, she will share it. Or-Gaule's control tries to force John to stab her, but Lunaeyes stands firm. John changes the attack to phantom form at the last instant and damages himself instead; Lunaeyes endures the lance's simulated impalement without crying out, walks forward along the weapon rather than retreating, embraces him, and tells him he has protected her. She promises to stay with him forever and help rebuild Quedland, then supports him until medical staff arrive.

key_events.summary: Calls John back, survives his phantom-form lance, and gives him a reason to live.

periods.summary: Lunaeyes does not appear directly in the chapter, but Or-Gaule reveals the price she paid to turn the conflict from a national clash into a representative war. After escaping Luxel with Alice's help, Lunaeyes returned by helicopter and proposed the League-rule war to avoid mass casualties. Or-Gaule initially refused because he did not care about League intervention, so Lunaeyes offered a grotesque incentive: if Vermillion lost and Quedland annexed it, she herself would execute the war criminals, meaning her parents and Stella. Or-Gaule accepted because the idea of Lunaeyes willingly killing loved ones promised exquisite emotional suffering. Stella realizes that Lunaeyes bore this nightmare alone to protect the people and directs her anger at Or-Gaule.

key_events.summary: Her self-sacrificial bargain with Or-Gaule is revealed as the reason the representative war happened.

periods.summary: The volume recalls that Lunaeyes's courage and judgment at Luxel prevented full-scale Vermillion-Quedland war by baiting Or-Gaule into a representative war, even though it forced her to wager her family if Vermillion lost. In the final battle, the teleport gates prepared by the White Wing Chancellor network let Vermillion and League forces appear when Or-Gaule violates the rules with civilian puppets. Lunaeyes rides with the wounded John through Divine Gate and supports him while he executes Or-Gaule with Circus Maximus. After the apparent victory, she remains at John's side as he breaks down over his failures and receives Stella's encouragement; her silent gaze tells John he is not alone. After the war she and John stand at the front line explaining the situation to Quedland's citizens. Stella reports that their marriage will be announced once the country stabilizes, and Lunaeyes will renounce her right to the Vermillion throne, making Stella the next successor.

key_events.summary: Supports John during Or-Gaule's execution and afterward through his grief.
Is reported to be leading Quedland recovery with John and renouncing succession through marriage.
